I use CMYK, 300 dpi images, bleed and crop marks, and outline fonts before sending.
I look at design work daily, try new styles and take short breaks.

video-editor.s: Video editor with 3 years of experience editing short-form social videos and YouTube content. I tell clear stories with pace, sound and simple graphics.
b: Edited 200+ short videos for brand social media.
Improved average watch time with tighter edits and captions.
Added motion graphics and colour correction.
Managed project files and versions neatly.
q: How do you edit for short attention spans?
Hook early and cut tightly.
How do you handle feedback?
Note it clearly and revise.
Which software do you use?
Name tools honestly.
How do you organise a project?
Folders and naming.
Show us your reel.
Bring a short best-of reel.
a: I start with a strong hook, keep cuts quick, add captions and remove anything that does not move the story.
I listen, ask questions if needed and make changes quickly.
Adobe Premiere Pro and After Effects, and DaVinci Resolve for colour.
I organise footage into folders, label clips and save versions often.
My reel shows short-form ads, YouTube videos and event highlights.

hr-business-partner.s: HR business partner with 12 years of experience supporting sales and technology leaders. I turn business plans into people plans: hiring, capability, performance and retention, backed by data.
b: Partnered with 4 business heads covering 1,800 employees across 6 locations.
Cut first-year attrition in the sales team from 38% to 24% with better hiring profiles and manager coaching.
Ran the annual performance and pay review cycle for the unit within budget and on time.
Built a monthly people dashboard (headcount, attrition, hiring, engagement) used in business reviews.
q: How is an HR business partner different from an HR generalist?
Show that you plan with the business, not just run HR tasks.
How do you handle a business head who disagrees with an HR policy?
Listen, explain the risk with facts, offer options within policy.
Tell me about a people problem you solved with data.
Name the metric, the cause you found, the action and the result.
How do you run a talent review?
Criteria, calibration, succession and follow-up actions.
How would you support a restructuring?
Plan, fairness, legal compliance, communication and care for people.
hr-business-partner.f: Not a fresher role. HR executives with 5 or more years usually move into it.
a: A generalist mostly runs HR processes well. As a business partner I sit in the business review, understand the plan for the year and turn it into a people plan: which roles we must hire, which skills we lack, where attrition hurts and who can step up. I still make sure the basics run, but my time goes to the decisions that move the business.

Our sales head wanted to skip the notice period buyout rule to hire faster. I listened first, then showed what the exception had cost us the last time, in pay disputes and in other managers asking for the same. I offered two options inside the policy: an earlier offer date and a joining bonus paid after six months. He chose the second and we closed the hire.

First-year attrition in our inside sales team was 38%. Exit data and stay interviews showed most leavers had been hired for the wrong shift pattern and had no clear target in their first month. We changed the hiring profile, added a 30-day ramp-up plan and coached team leads. Attrition fell to 24% within a year.

I agree the criteria with the business head first, usually performance and potential with examples. Managers rate their people, then we calibrate together so one strict manager does not pull ratings down. For each critical role we name ready-now and ready-later successors, and every high-potential person gets one development action with a date. I check those actions every quarter.

I would agree the business reason and the new structure with leadership, check every step against labour law and company policy, and make sure selection is based on clear, fair criteria. Managers get a script and training before people are told. Affected employees hear it in person, with their support package and help with outplacement, and the people who stay get honest answers about what changes.

area-sales-manager.s: Area sales manager with 11 years in FMCG and consumer durables. I lead distributor and field teams to hit volume, coverage and collection targets across a territory.
b: Led a team of 9 sales officers and 14 distributors across 3 districts in Karnataka.
Grew area sales from Rs 18 crore to Rs 26 crore in two years while keeping distributor ROI healthy.
Raised outlet coverage by 35% with a beat plan review and new rural distributors.
Brought outstanding beyond 30 days down from 22% to 9% of receivables.
q: How do you plan your monthly target across the team?
Split by outlet potential, past sales and new outlets, then review weekly.
A distributor is underperforming. What do you do?
Find the cause with data, agree a plan, and replace only after support fails.
How do you motivate a sales officer who keeps missing target?
Joint field visits, coaching on one or two gaps, clear review dates.
How do you handle high outstanding in the market?
Credit discipline, regular follow-up, stop supply rules applied fairly.
Tell me about a new territory you opened.
Market study, distributor choice, first 90 days and numbers.
area-sales-manager.f: Not a fresher role. Sales officers and territory managers grow into it.
a: I split the area target by outlet potential, last year's sales and the new outlets we plan to open, not just equally by head. Each sales officer gets a weekly number and a list of focus outlets and SKUs. Every Monday we review the last week's secondary sales and fix gaps before they grow.

I look at the numbers first: secondary sales, stock age, outlet coverage, claims and payments. Then I meet the distributor to understand the cause, whether it is cash, manpower or our own supply. We agree a 60-day plan with clear targets. If nothing changes after real support, I bring in a second distributor or replace him, with a proper hand-over so the market is not hurt.

I go to the market with him for two or three days to see what happens at the outlet. Usually the gap is one or two things, such as poor beat discipline or not pitching new SKUs. We agree on those, I review them every week, and I recognise improvement in front of the team. If there is still no progress after a fair time, I follow the formal performance process.

I keep credit limits and days agreed with each distributor, track outstanding every week and visit the large overdue accounts myself. Stopping supply is the last step, applied the same way for everyone. In my last area this brought outstanding beyond 30 days from 22% to 9% of receivables in two quarters.

When we entered two new districts I first mapped outlet counts, competitor presence and wholesale points. We chose distributors with their own vans and good credit history, set up beats for 600 outlets and ran a launch scheme for the first 90 days. The area reached Rs 1.2 crore a month within six months.

key-account-manager.s: Key account manager with 9 years handling large retail and B2B customers. I grow share of business with each account through joint plans, service and trusted relationships.
b: Managed 6 national accounts worth Rs 40 crore a year.
Grew the top account by 28% with a joint business plan and quarterly reviews.
Negotiated annual terms and promotions within the agreed margin.
Set up a monthly service review that cut order fill issues by half.
q: How do you build a plan for a key account?
Account goals, your goals, growth levers and a review rhythm.
A key customer asks for a bigger discount. How do you respond?
Trade value for value, protect margin, escalate with facts.
How do you handle a service failure with a big account?
Own it fast, fix it, explain the cause and prevent repeats.
How do you grow an account that seems saturated?
New categories, new locations, better shelf or service levels.
Which numbers do you track for each account?
Sales, margin, share of business, fill rate and collections.
key-account-manager.f: Not a fresher role. Sales executives with account experience move into it.
a: I start with the customer's own goals for the year, such as growth in a category or better margin, and set them beside ours. Then I list the growth levers: distribution, promotions, new products and supply service. We agree a joint business plan with numbers and owners, and review it every quarter with both teams.

I never give a discount without getting something back. I ask what the extra discount must achieve, then offer value in return, such as more display space, a bigger order or a longer agreement. If the gap is still large I take it to my manager with the account P&L, so the decision is based on numbers.

I call the customer the same day, own the problem and give a clear recovery plan, for example an emergency dispatch. After that I find the real cause with our supply team and share it with the customer along with what we changed. Being honest quickly usually makes the relationship stronger.

I look for growth outside the current base: categories they do not list yet, stores or cities where we are thin, better shelf placement or new pack sizes for their shoppers. With one retail account, adding a value pack for their smaller-town stores grew our sales with them by 28%.
Sales against plan, margin after trade terms, our share of their category, order fill rate and on-time delivery, and collections. I review these monthly and share the main ones with the customer too.

finance-manager.s: Finance manager and chartered accountant with 13 years in manufacturing and services. I run closing, budgeting, compliance and cash so leaders can decide with clear numbers.
b: Ran the monthly close for 3 entities in 5 working days, down from 9.
Led the annual budget and rolling forecast for a Rs 450 crore business.
Managed statutory audit, GST and income tax compliance with no major findings.
Freed Rs 12 crore of working capital by tightening receivables and inventory.
q: How do you speed up the month-end close?
Calendar, owners, reconciliations through the month and fewer manual entries.
Tell me about a budget variance you explained to management.
Cause, impact, action, and how forecasting changed after.
How do you manage working capital?
Receivable days, inventory days, payable terms and a weekly cash view.
How do you prepare for a statutory audit?
Clean schedules, early review of judgement areas and open points closed on time.
How do you handle a GST notice?
Read it carefully, reconcile the data, reply on time with documents, and get advice when needed.
finance-manager.f: Not a fresher role. Accountants and CAs with 5 or more years move into it.
a: I publish a close calendar with an owner and a deadline for every task. Bank, vendor and inter-company reconciliations are done through the month, not at the end. We cut manual journals by using recurring entries and system accruals. Those steps took our close from 9 working days to 5.

Material costs were 6% above budget in one quarter. I split the variance into price, usage and mix, and found most of it came from a supplier price rise we had not built into the budget. I showed management the impact, the purchasing team renegotiated, and we moved to a rolling forecast with monthly price updates.

I track receivable days, inventory days and payable days every month, and look at cash weekly. We tightened credit approvals, followed up overdue customers with sales, cut slow-moving stock and aligned vendor terms with our cash cycle. That released Rs 12 crore in a year.

I agree the timeline with the auditors early and prepare clean schedules for every balance. I review areas that need judgement, such as provisions and revenue recognition, before they arrive. Any open point gets an owner and a date. Our last two audits closed on time with no major findings.

I read the notice carefully to understand exactly what is asked and the due date. Then I reconcile our returns with the books and the portal data, prepare the documents and reply before the deadline. If the matter is complex I bring in our tax consultant, and I note the cause so it does not happen again.

it-project-manager.s: IT project manager with 11 years delivering software and infrastructure projects for banking and retail clients. I keep scope, time, cost and quality under control with clear plans and honest reporting.
b: Delivered a core system migration for a bank with 40 people across 3 vendors, on budget.
Ran 4 agile teams with 2-week sprints and a shared release plan.
Cut open critical defects at go-live from 31 to 3 with an earlier test plan.
Kept a RAID log and weekly status report trusted by the steering committee.
q: How do you handle scope creep?
Change requests with impact on time and cost, agreed by the sponsor.
A project is two weeks late. What do you do?
Find the critical path issue, options to recover, and tell stakeholders early.
How do you run agile and waterfall work together?
Common milestones, a release plan and clear hand-offs.
How do you manage a difficult vendor?
Contract, facts, regular reviews and escalation steps.
What goes into your status report?
RAG status, progress, risks, issues, decisions needed.
it-project-manager.f: Not a fresher role. Developers, testers and coordinators grow into it.
a: Every new request goes through a simple change process. I write down the impact on time, cost and risk and take it to the sponsor to decide. Small items can go into a later release. This keeps the team focused and the sponsor in control of trade-offs.

I first find the exact cause on the critical path, for example a delayed interface from a vendor. Then I look at options: adding people, running tasks in parallel, or reducing scope for the first release. I tell stakeholders early with the facts and a recommended option, rather than hoping to catch up quietly.

Agile teams plan in sprints, but the business still needs fixed dates for things like data migration or training. I keep a shared release plan with common milestones, agree what each team must deliver by each date, and hold a weekly cross-team meeting to manage dependencies.

I go back to the contract and the agreed service levels, and use facts such as missed dates and defect counts. We hold a regular review with the vendor's delivery head and agree a fix plan. If there is still no change, I escalate through the steps in the contract. I keep it professional, because we usually still need them.

Overall status in red, amber or green, progress against milestones, budget used, top risks and issues with owners, and any decisions I need from the steering committee. I keep it to one page so people actually read it.

digital-marketing-manager.s: Digital marketing manager with 10 years in D2C and education brands. I plan and run performance, SEO, content and CRM programmes that bring leads and sales at a cost the business can afford.
b: Managed a Rs 6 crore yearly ad budget across search, social and video.
Cut cost per lead by 32% with better audiences, landing pages and tracking.
Grew organic traffic 3 times in 18 months through technical SEO and content.
Built email and WhatsApp journeys that lifted repeat purchase by 18%.
q: How do you decide the budget split across channels?
Past cost per result, funnel role of each channel, and test budget.
Cost per lead doubled last month. How do you find out why?
Check tracking, audience, creative, landing page and auction changes.
How do you measure the return on brand campaigns?
Search lift, direct traffic, assisted conversions and surveys.
How do you run an A/B test on a landing page?
One change, enough traffic, a set period, then decide.
How do you manage agencies and an in-house team?
Clear goals, shared dashboards and regular reviews.
digital-marketing-manager.f: Not a fresher role. Digital marketing executives grow into it.
a: I look at the past cost per lead or sale for each channel and the role it plays: search captures demand, social and video create it. Most of the budget goes to what is proven, about 10 to 15% goes to tests, and I move money every two weeks based on results.

First I check that tracking still works, because a broken tag can look like a cost rise. Then I look at what changed: audience, creatives, landing page speed, bids or more competition in the auction. I fix the biggest cause first and watch daily until the cost settles.

I agree the measures before the campaign starts: branded search volume, direct traffic, assisted conversions and, where the budget allows, a brand lift survey. I compare regions or periods with and without the campaign where I can.

I change one thing at a time, such as the headline or the form length. I decide the sample size and run time in advance, keep both versions live together, and only call a winner when the result is clear. Then I record the learning for the next test.

Each agency and team member has clear goals and budgets. We share one dashboard so everyone sees the same numbers, hold weekly working sessions and a monthly review against goals. I keep strategy and measurement in-house.

brand-manager.s: Brand manager with 9 years in personal care and foods. I own brand plans, launches and P&L, using consumer insight to grow market share.
b: Owned a Rs 120 crore brand P&L and grew it 14% in a flat category.
Launched 5 new variants, with 2 reaching Rs 10 crore in the first year.
Ran consumer research that led to a pack redesign and a 2-point share gain.
Worked with sales on trade plans for modern trade and e-commerce.
q: Walk me through a launch you led.
Insight, proposition, mix, launch plan and results.
Market share is falling. Where do you start?
Data by channel, region and pack, then consumer reasons.
How do you brief a creative agency?
One clear task, insight, audience and what success looks like.
How do you decide a price increase?
Cost, competitor prices, consumer value and volume risk.
How do you work with sales?
Joint plans, field visits and shared numbers.
brand-manager.f: Not a fresher role. Management trainees in marketing grow into it.
a: Consumer research showed young parents wanted a gentle soap that also smelt fresh. We built a variant around that, tested the name and pack, priced it at a small premium, and planned TV, digital and in-store sampling together with sales. It reached Rs 10 crore in the first year.

I look at share data by region, channel and pack size to find where we are losing. Then I talk to consumers and the sales team to understand why: price, availability, a competitor offer or a tired product. The fix depends on the cause.
I give the agency one clear task, the consumer insight, the target audience, the one thing we want people to feel or do, and how we will measure success. I avoid long lists of messages.

I look at our cost increase, competitor prices, how much consumers value the brand and how sensitive volume has been to past price changes. Sometimes a smaller pack or a new price point works better than a straight increase.
I build trade plans together with sales, visit markets with the field team and share the same numbers. When sales understand the plan and believe in it, launches go much better.

information-technology.i: IT recruiters scan for your tech stack, the size of what you built and proof that it worked. A project line with a clear result beats a long list of tools.
h: Tech stack named in each project
Links to code or live work
information-technology.cl: I am applying for the Software Engineer role on your payments team. Over the last 3 years I have built and run REST services in Java and Spring Boot, and I enjoy the part of the job where a slow or broken system becomes fast and reliable again.
information-technology.fr: I am a final-year B.Tech student applying for the Graduate Engineer Trainee role. In my final-year project I built a library management web app in Python and Django that our college now uses, and I enjoy debugging until something works properly.
mx: Listing every language you have heard of instead of the ones the job needs
No link to GitHub, a portfolio or a live project
Copying the same letter for a product company and a services company

engineering.i: Engineering recruiters look for the tools you use, the processes you know and your shop-floor or site exposure. Mention plants, products and standards by name.
engineering.cl: I am writing to apply for the Mechanical Engineer position at your plant. In 3 years of design and production support I have designed fixtures that cut setup time and led root cause analysis that closed repeat quality issues.
engineering.fr: I am writing to apply for the Graduate Engineer Trainee post. During my 6-week internship at an auto components plant I studied changeover times on a press line and suggested a quick-change die setup that the team is now testing.
mx: Not naming the standards and software you know, such as GD&T or SolidWorks
Talking about theory without any shop-floor or site exposure
Skipping safety, which plant managers look for first

accounting-finance.i: Finance recruiters check accuracy, compliance knowledge and the tools you use. GST, TDS, reconciliation and closing experience should be easy to spot.
accounting-finance.cl: I am applying for the Accountant role in your finance team. I have 4 years of experience filing GST and TDS returns on time, closing books every month and supporting statutory audits without major observations.
accounting-finance.fr: I am a B.Com graduate applying for the Junior Accountant role. During my articleship I helped prepare GST returns for 15 clients and reconciled bank statements every month, and I am comfortable with Tally Prime and Excel.
mx: Not mentioning GST, TDS or audit work, which recruiters scan for
Spelling or number errors, which hurt more in finance than anywhere else
Writing about wanting to learn without showing what you already know

sales.i: Sales recruiters want numbers first: target achievement, deal size, new accounts and territory. Show consistency over many months, not one lucky deal.
sales.cl: I am writing to apply for the Sales Executive role. In the last financial year I achieved 110% of my target and opened 35 new business accounts by following up steadily and understanding what each client needed.
sales.fr: I am applying for the Sales Trainee role. As the sponsorship lead for my college fest I called 60 local businesses and raised ₹75,000, which taught me how to listen to what a buyer wants before I pitch.
mx: No numbers: target, achievement or accounts
Talking about yourself instead of the customer and the territory
Ending without asking for a meeting

marketing.i: Marketing recruiters look for channels you have run, budgets you have handled and the results you can prove. Name the metrics you moved.
marketing.cl: I am applying for the Digital Marketing Executive role. Over 2 years I have grown organic traffic for an e-commerce brand through on-page SEO and steady content, and managed monthly ad budgets with a focus on cost per lead.
marketing.fr: I am applying for the Marketing Intern role. I run the Instagram page for our college club and grew it from 300 to 2,400 followers in a year by posting short videos twice a week and replying to every comment.
mx: Saying "creative" without showing any campaign or result
Ignoring the channel the job is about, such as SEO or performance ads
Not linking a portfolio or sample work

human-resources.i: HR recruiters check hiring volume, HR operations, compliance and the tools you use. Show that you can be trusted with people data.
human-resources.cl: I am writing to apply for the HR Executive role. In 3 years I have closed more than 60 positions a year and run onboarding for every new joiner, from documents to induction.
human-resources.fr: I am an MBA (HR) student applying for the HR Trainee role. During my summer internship I screened over 400 resumes and scheduled 90 interviews for a BPO, and I learned how much candidates value a quick reply.
mx: Talking only about "liking people" without hiring or operations examples
Not mentioning HRMS, ATS or Excel skills
Sharing confidential details from a past employer as examples

education.i: Schools and colleges check subjects, classes taught, board or university, qualifications and results. Activities and parent communication also matter.
e: CBSE, ICSE and state board schools
education.cl: I am applying for the post of Mathematics Teacher. For 5 years I have taught classes 6 to 10 in a CBSE school, using activity-based lessons to help weaker students catch up.
education.fr: I am applying for the post of Primary Teacher. I completed my B.Ed with a 6-week teaching practice in class 3, where I used picture cards and group reading to help slow readers, and I have cleared CTET.
mx: Not naming the subjects, classes and board you can teach
Leaving out eligibility such as B.Ed, CTET or state TET
No example of how you handle students who need extra help

government.i: Government recruitment usually follows the official notification. For contract roles, PSUs and interviews, a clear resume with exact dates, qualifications and duties helps.
government.cl: I am writing to apply for the contract post in your department. I have 2 years of experience in office administration, record keeping and data entry on government portals.
government.fr: I am writing to apply for the contract post of Data Entry Operator advertised in your notification. I hold a B.A. and a DCA certificate, type at 40 words per minute in English and Hindi, and have used government portals during my internship at the block office.
mx: Ignoring the format given in the official notification
Missing exact dates, qualifications or reference numbers
Writing a long personal story instead of eligibility and skills

retail.i: Retail recruiters look for customer service, sales targets, billing accuracy and shift flexibility. Store size and footfall help them picture your work.
retail.cl: I am applying for the Retail Sales Associate role. I have 2 years of experience on a busy fashion store floor, helping 50 or more customers a day and meeting my monthly targets in most months.
retail.fr: I am applying for the Retail Sales Associate role at your store. I have helped at my family’s clothing shop on weekends for 3 years, handling billing, stock and customers during festival rush.
mx: Not mentioning availability for weekends and festive seasons
No example of helping a customer or meeting a target
Forgetting to mention languages spoken in the store’s area

legal.i: Legal recruiters check practice areas, courts or forums, drafting experience and the kind of clients you have served. Confidentiality matters, so describe matters in general terms.
legal.cl: I am writing to apply for the Associate position in your litigation team. In 4 years of practice I have drafted pleadings in civil and commercial matters and appeared before district courts and tribunals.
legal.fr: I am a final-year LL.B student applying for the Junior Associate role. During my internship at a civil litigation chamber I drafted 8 applications, researched case law on SCC Online and attended hearings at the district court.
mx: Not naming the practice areas you have worked in
Long legal language where plain words would do
Typos, which make a reader doubt your drafting

maintenance-repair.i: Maintenance recruiters look for your trade, machines handled, safety practice and breakdown records. Name the equipment you know.
maintenance-repair.cl: I am applying for the Maintenance Technician role. I am an ITI Fitter with 5 years of experience in preventive and breakdown maintenance of CNC and textile machines.
maintenance-repair.fr: I am an ITI Fitter applying for the Maintenance Technician post. During my apprenticeship at a packaging plant I carried out daily preventive maintenance on 6 machines and learned lock-out tag-out procedures.
mx: Not listing the machines and systems you have worked on
Leaving out your trade certificate or licence
No mention of safety practice

administrative.i: Office and support roles are judged on reliability, accuracy, communication and computer skills. Typing speed, languages and tools should be easy to find.
administrative.cl: I am writing to apply for the Administrative Assistant role. For 4 years I have managed calendars, travel and records for senior managers, so that they could focus on their work.
administrative.fr: I am applying for the Office Assistant role. I completed a B.Com and an MS Office course, type at 35 words per minute, and handled the visitor register and phone calls during a 3-month internship at a CA firm.
mx: Not giving typing speed, software or languages
No example of handling volume, such as calls or records a day
A long letter for a role that values short, clear writing

real-estate.i: Real estate recruiters look for units sold or managed, project types and local market knowledge. Honest dealing with buyers is valued.
real-estate.cl: I am applying for the Sales Executive role for your residential projects. In 2 years I have closed the sale of more than 30 apartments by understanding buyer needs and following up patiently.
real-estate.fr: I am applying for the Sales Trainee role in your residential projects. I have lived in this area for 10 years, know its schools, transport and markets well, and enjoy explaining options clearly to families.
mx: No local market knowledge
Over-promising returns, which buyers and employers distrust
Not mentioning follow-up habits or a CRM

production.i: Production recruiters check the industry, processes, output and quality results, and safety. Standards such as GMP or 5S should be visible.
production.cl: I am writing to apply for the Production Officer role. I have 4 years of experience in oral solid dosage manufacturing and I keep batch records right first time.
production.fr: I am a Diploma holder in Mechanical Engineering applying for the Production Trainee post. During my in-plant training I helped the team track hourly output on a packing line and learned 5S and GMP basics.
mx: Not naming processes and equipment you have handled
No output, quality or safety numbers
Ignoring shift work, which most plants expect

business-management.i: Management recruiters look for the scope you handled (team, budget, products) and the outcomes you drove. Show decisions, not only duties.
business-management.cl: I am applying for the Product Manager role. For 4 years I have worked with engineering and design teams to ship features that solved real user problems and moved clear metrics.
business-management.fr: I am an MBA graduate applying for the Management Trainee programme. In my summer internship at a logistics firm I analysed route costs for 40 trucks and suggested two changes that the team adopted, saving about 6% a month.
mx: General talk about leadership with no team size or budget
No decision you made and its result
Repeating the resume instead of explaining why this company

security-protective-services.i: Security employers check training, alertness, discipline and the type of premises you have guarded. Ex-servicemen should mention service details.
security-protective-services.cl: I am writing to apply for the Security Guard position. I have 5 years of experience guarding corporate offices and residential complexes and I keep every register complete.
security-protective-services.fr: I am applying for the post of Security Guard. I have completed PSARA-approved security training and a fire safety course, and I served as a volunteer marshal at district sports events.

Not saying the premises types you can guard
No mention of shift availability

hospitality-catering.i: Hospitality recruiters check departments worked, property size, guest feedback and grooming. Industrial training details help freshers.
hospitality-catering.cl: I am applying for the Front Office Executive role. For 3 years I have handled check-ins, guest requests and complaints at a 120-room hotel and helped improve our review scores.
hospitality-catering.fr: I am a hotel management graduate applying for the Front Office Associate role. During industrial training at a 4-star hotel I handled check-ins, guest requests and Opera PMS, and I speak English, Hindi and basic French.

transport-logistics.i: Logistics recruiters look for volumes handled, on-time delivery, inventory accuracy and the systems you use.
transport-logistics.cl: I am writing to apply for the Logistics Executive role. I plan daily dispatches for more than 40 shipments and work closely with transporters to deliver on time.
transport-logistics.fr: I am a B.Com graduate applying for the Logistics Trainee role. During my internship at a distribution centre I tracked 150 dispatches a day in Excel and learned how e-way bills and delivery challans are prepared.

Not mentioning ERP or WMS tools
Missing accuracy or on-time numbers

transportation.cl: I am applying for the Driver position. I have 8 years of commercial driving experience and a clean record on both city and highway routes.
transportation.fr: I am applying for the post of Driver. I hold a valid LMV licence with a commercial badge, have driven for 3 years without any accident, and know the routes across the city well.

No mention of safety record

medical.i: Healthcare recruiters check registration, qualifications, departments worked, patient load and emergency skills. Certifications such as BLS should be clear.
medical.cl: I am writing to apply for the Staff Nurse position. I hold a B.Sc in Nursing and have 4 years of experience in medical-surgical and ICU wards, with a strong focus on medication safety.
medical.fr: I am a B.Sc Nursing graduate applying for the Staff Nurse post. During my internship I worked in medical, surgical and paediatric wards, and I hold BLS certification and state nursing council registration.
mx: Missing registration number and certifications
Not naming departments and patient load
Using abbreviations that a hospital HR team may not know

sport-fitness.i: Fitness employers look for certifications, client results and the kinds of training you run.
sport-fitness.cl: I am applying for the Personal Trainer role. I am certified and have trained 25 personal clients with plans built around their goals and safety.
sport-fitness.fr: I am a certified fitness trainer applying for the Personal Trainer role. During my internship at a gym I helped 15 members with form and planned beginner programmes, and I hold CPR certification.
mx: Not naming your certification
No client results

more: Ran daily toolbox talks for 40 workers; the site had zero lost-time injuries in 14 months.

ex: Prioritised tasks well.
Triaged 25 support tickets a day by business impact, meeting the response-time target.

Sequenced 50 daily orders by delivery date, cutting late dispatches by a third.
Organised the director’s calendar and travel, clearing 15 to 20 meeting requests a week.

more: Raised class 10 maths pass rate from 78% to 94% in one year.

Field sales professional with 4 years in FMCG, managing 120 outlets.

Scored 92% in class 12 and 8.7 CGPA in B.Tech.

ex: Investigated quality issues.
Diagnosed the cause of repeat defects with 5-Why analysis and cut scrap on the line.
more: Analysed 150 complaints a month and found 3 causes behind 70% of them.
Examined 2 years of vendor payments and recovered ₹4.2 lakh in duplicate claims.
Diagnosed recurring motor trips and fixed the cause, cutting downtime by 20 hours a month.
investigate.ok: For compliance, audit and quality roles, followed by the finding.

ex: Innovative thinker.
Designed a new fixture that cut setup time on 2 machining lines.
more: Created activity-based maths kits now used by 6 teachers in the school.
Started a WhatsApp catalogue that brought 22% of monthly orders.
Designed a low-cost jig that removed a manual measuring step.
innovative.ok: Avoid as a self-description. Describe the new thing you made and what it did.

ex: Leading a team.
Managing a team of 12 sales executives across 3 cities.
more: Heading a 9-person sales team that grew revenue 18% this year.
Directing 3 ERP roll-outs at the same time for clients in retail and pharma.
Supervising a 25-person night shift with the plant’s best safety record.
leading.ok: When the size of the team or project follows it.

ex: Good teamwork skills.
Worked with design and engineering to ship 12 features in a year.
more: Worked with design and sales to launch a product range in 6 weeks.
Covered shifts for 2 colleagues during peak season so the store stayed fully staffed.
Partnered with the QA team to cut release bugs by 40%.
teamwork.ok: Fine in a skills list, but show it in an experience line with who you worked with and the result.

strategy.m: A plan to reach a goal.
ex: Worked on marketing strategy.
Built the 6-month content roadmap from keyword research.
more: Planned a 6-month content roadmap that doubled organic sign-ups.
Built a territory plan for 3 new districts, adding ₹45 lakh in annual sales.
Proposed shifting 20% of ad spend to search, which cut cost per lead by 30%.
strategy.ok: For senior roles, when you name the plan, the goal and the result.

ex: Built a dashboard.
Designed a weekly sales dashboard that replaced 6 manual reports.
more: Grew a network of 40 distributors across Gujarat.
Designed a Power BI dashboard used daily by 25 managers.
Hired and trained a 12-person support team in 4 months.
build.ok: Good for anything you made from scratch. Add what it does or who uses it.

skilled.m: Good at a task through practice.
ex: Skilled in Excel.
Proficient in Excel: pivot tables, XLOOKUP and automated monthly MIS reports.
more: Advanced Excel: pivot tables, XLOOKUP, macros; automated 5 weekly reports.
Licensed electrician with 7 years in industrial panels and motor control.
Presented monthly results to the leadership team for 2 years.
skilled.ok: In a skills heading. In a line about you, prove the skill instead.

ex: Helped customers.
Resolved 60+ customer chats a day within quality targets.
more: Resolved 60 customer chats a day with a 4.7 out of 5 rating.
Prepared weekly sales reports for the area manager across 18 stores.
Guided 30 final-year students through their project reports.
help.ok: When helping others is the main duty, but still say how many and with what result.

manage.m: Being in charge of people, money or work.
ex: Managed the warehouse.
Supervised a 25-person warehouse team and raised stock accuracy with cycle counts.
more: Oversaw 35 key accounts worth ₹3 crore a year.
Ran stock for 1,200 SKUs with 99% accuracy in quarterly audits.
Ran Instagram and LinkedIn for a brand, growing followers from 2,000 to 15,000.
manage.ok: Fine when you were in charge, followed by the scope: people, money or volume.

ex: Improved website speed.
Optimised the home page and raised its performance score from 58 to 91.
more: Raised the customer satisfaction score from 78% to 91% in 6 months.
Cut month-end closing from 8 days to 4 by standardising journal templates.
Increased average bill value by 15% through add-on suggestions.
improve.ok: It is a fine word when a number follows. Without one, it says little.

responsible-for.m: A duty that was yours to do.
ex: Responsible for payroll.
Owned monthly payroll inputs for 250 employees with no late payments.
more: Handled billing for 400 customers a day with zero cash differences in 6 months.
Owned hiring for 3 departments, closing 70 positions in a year.
Ran safety for a 200-worker site with no reportable incidents.
responsible-for.ok: Avoid it. It lists a duty, not what you did. Start with the action instead.

worked-on.m: Being part of a task or project.
ex: Worked on the annual budget.
Prepared the annual budget model for 4 business units.
more: Built the login and payments screens for an app with 50,000 downloads.
Produced 12 monthly MIS reports for the finance head.
Delivered the electrical design for a 6-floor commercial building.
worked-on.ok: Rarely. Name the exact part you did.

ex: Good communication skills.
Briefed senior leaders weekly on project status and risks.
more: Briefed 10 clients a week on order status and resolved delivery issues.
Fluent in English, Hindi and Tamil; handled customer calls in all three.
Liaised between design, production and sales for 15 product launches.
communicate.ok: In a skills list. In experience lines, say who you communicated with and why.

detail-oriented.m: Careful and accurate with small things.
ex: Detail-oriented person.
Entered 500+ records a day with very few errors found in quality checks.
more: Found and reversed ₹2.1 lakh in duplicate vendor entries during reconciliation.
Entered 8,000 records a month with 99.8% accuracy.
Prepared print-ready files for 40 jobs with no printer rework.
detail-oriented.ok: Show it with an accuracy rate or an error you caught instead.

ex: Hard-working employee.
Handled 80+ calls a shift while keeping quality scores above target.
more: Made 60 calls a day and visited 8 outlets daily, the highest activity in the team.
Worked part-time 20 hours a week while keeping an 8.2 CGPA.
Covered extra shifts during the festive season, helping the store reach 120% of target.
hardworking.ok: Avoid it. Everyone writes it. Show effort with a number.
